paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: nobody out-questions Jesus. Two different groups showed up with two different traps, and both walked away with nothing. The spies came with flattery and a coin, the Sadducees came with a seven-brother riddle, and Jesus saw through both (Luke 20:23). So if you ever feel like a question is too tricky to bring to Him, remember He's not the one who gets cornered.

Now look at the coin. Jesus says, "Give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's" (Luke 20:25). Caesar's image was on the denarius, and people are made in God's image (Genesis 1:27), so that means YOU, friend, and every person you meet. I'd say the better question is not what you owe the tax office, it's whether you've handed God what is His.

Then the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, hit Him with the widow and her seven husbands, and Jesus gives them the quiet answer: God "is not the God of the dead, but of the living, for to Him all are alive" (Luke 20:38). Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are still called His, so death does not get the last word on anybody who belongs to Him. That's why I keep my ovens ready for the Marriage Supper of the Lamb, because the promise is real, and the age to come is better than anything we're arguing about here. Take your questions to Jesus, give Him what's His, and hold on to that hope.
